correctness.rationale: Affine invariance reduces to barycentric coordinates. A plane through the tetrahedron centroid has coefficient sum zero, so the exhaustive sign types are \(1+3\), \(2+2\), and boundary cases with zero coefficients. In the triangular \(1+3\) case, centroid coordinate \(1/4\) forces all three opposite coefficient magnitudes equal, yielding a facet-parallel plane. In the \(2+2\) case, the exact quadrilateral centroid equations reduce to polynomials \(P,Q\); a fresh independent SymPy reconstruction gives resultant \(16384u^3(u-1)^6(u+1)^9(3u^2-4)\), so the admissible common zero is \(u=0\), and then \(P(0,v)=v^2(3v^2-4)\) forces \(v=0\). Boundary sign cases cannot have all barycentric centroid coordinates equal to one quarter. Thus exactly four singleton/triple and three pair/pair partitions remain.
correctness.risk: The result is three-dimensional only; the exact algebraic bottleneck is the quadrilateral-centroid elimination, independently reproduced here.

final_claim: Every nondegenerate tetrahedron has exactly seven unoriented planes through its centroid whose planar-section centroid is the same point: in barycentric coordinates they are the four planes \(\lambda_i=1/4\) and the three planes \(\lambda_i+\lambda_j=1/2\).
limitations: No claim for arbitrary interior base points or higher-dimensional simplices.
